questions.question_text:
What is the difference between:
a) random sampling and systematic sampling?
b) primary and secondary data?

marking_scheme.rubric: AO1: Define sampling and data types.
keywords_required: a) Random sampling means every item/person has an equal chance of being selected (e.g. using a random number generator). Systematic sampling is taking samples at regular intervals (e.g. every 10 metres or every 5th person).
b) Primary data is collected firsthand by the researcher (e.g. fieldwork). Secondary data is pre-existing data collected by someone else (e.g. internet research, census data).

questions.question_text: Suggest a method to accurately measure the width and depth of a river at several points. [4]

keywords_required: Width: Stretch a measuring tape horizontally across the river from bank to bank, keeping it taut.
Depth: Use a metre ruler/ranging pole.
Measure the depth at regular systematic intervals across the width (e.g. every 0.5m).
Ensure the ruler is placed vertically on the river bed and read the depth where the water hits the ruler.

questions.question_text:
Read the scenario: A group of students is conducting fieldwork near a river. They are collecting data using transects and taking photographs. They notice the riverbank is steep, and one student has a bee allergy.
a) Identify three potential risks in this scenario.
b) Suggest three ways the group can address these risks to ensure safety during their fieldwork.

keywords_required: a) Slipping on the steep bank, drowning/falling into the water, bee sting (anaphylactic shock).
b) Wear sturdy footwear with good grip, work in groups/never enter water alone, ensure the student carries an EpiPen/medication and others know how to use it.
